claims.text: ADR 0028 runs reconciliation once a day; results come before the next working morning (assumed, confirmed by accounting); one job and one report fetched; the report also catches refunds made outside Đơn Hàng; a difference can sit unnoticed up to a day.

Rejected option: asking the gateway about each refund right after sending finds a lost answer sooner, but adds one call per refund and does not see refunds made outside Đơn Hàng, so it cannot replace the report.

YC-10 asks for at least 24 hours of automatic resending before staff take over; RefundSettings defaults are FirstRetryDelay 1 minute, MaxRetryDelay 1 hour, GiveUpAfter 24 hours. The lab's Compose file shortens only the two delays (2 s and 10 s); GiveUpAfter stays 24 hours.

claims.text: RefundSender resends with the same key; the design assumes, as the lab's fake gateway does, that a key the gateway has seen gets its earlier answer and nothing is refunded again, so a retry that reaches the gateway within the window ends the row refunded.
claims.source_hint: fake-gateway/Program.cs @ stage-4 lines 1-5, 66-75; docs/design/refund-design.md lines 42-44, 95-96 (risk R2); DonHang.Payments/RefundSender.cs lines 88-97

claims.text: RecordResult marks a refund row failed when the gateway refuses it or once GiveUpAfter has passed since the request, and sends payment.refund-failed; on that message the API returns the order to paid, even if the gateway did refund.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Payments/RefundSender.cs @ stage-4 lines 99-105; docs/design/refund-design.md line 56; docs/design/reconciliation-design-review.md lines 53, 88

claims.text: Review trade-off point on the 24-hour window: longer means fewer failed rows the gateway in fact refunded, but orders stay refunding longer and staff wait longer; the review keeps 24 hours.
Review trade-off point on frequency: once a day is one job and one report, but a difference can sit up to a day; driver 2 (each difference found within a day) is 'vừa đủ', just met.

Hand correction is slower than the job correcting, but staff propose and accounting approves (assumed roles), so no one both makes and approves a change to money (driver 3); corrections go to the audit log.
Report lines and each run's result are kept as long as the refund rows (assumed), as evidence for accounting, at the cost of storage.
Trusting only the gateway's answer for each call, as stage-3 does, leaves no second record to compare, against driver 1, every difference is explained (goal 2 of refund-requirements.md in the ADR).
ADR 0028's feedback section: accounting asked whether the job could fix clear differences; no, money rows are corrected by a person and approved by another; the decision did not change.
Stage-4 has no reconciliation code; ADR 0028's header says so.

ADR 0028 is reviewed again when refunds per day grow far beyond a small batch (or a second gateway is added); the estimate is about 1,000 refunds on the busiest day (assumed) and the review finds no load bottleneck.
Gateway A lets its refund history be exported as CSV at any time (via admin page and API); a gateway refund made by hand on the gateway's admin page has no row in Payments (ĐS-2).
Staff take over a refund only once its row is failed, i.e. after the retry window (YC-10 'trước khi chuyển cho nhân viên xử lý').

Where a day's unnoticed difference costs more than one extra call per refund (e.g. large refunds), a team could add the per-refund check beside the report, while keeping the report for refunds made by hand.
claims.source_hint: derived from review lines 72-73 and ADR 0028 lines 25-27

claims.text: If driver 2 becomes one hour, only the frequency line is reopened; more frequent runs each fetch a report and the wait-one-more-run rule for missing rows needs weighing again.
claims.source_hint: derived from review lines 75-76; ADR 0028 lines 43-45

claims.text: Raising GiveUpAfter to 72 hours is allowed by YC-10 (at least 24 hours) but keeps orders refunding up to three days and staff waiting; 12 hours breaks YC-10; a longer window never removes the need for the report.
A job knows only that two records differ, not which is right; a rule rewriting money rows is a change nobody approved case by case, against separation of duties and driver 3.
